channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: [8] Nonlinear responses induced by inhomogeneous edge states in a centrosymmetric topological insulator
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Yan Li, Peng Li

Authors: Yitian Guo, Chengxin Jiang, Chenxi Liu, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Investigation of topological edge states in ZrTe5, relevant to user's topological materials focus.

Tags: #ZrTe5 #topologicalinsulator #edgestates

Abstract: Second-order electrical nonlinearity is conventionally thought to originate in crystals with noncentrosymmetric lattices or magnetic order. Here, the authors show another generation paradigm in bulk centrosymmetric, nonmagnetic ZrTe5, arising from an inhomogeneous surface edge-state distribution.
